question: Which uptime, heartbeat, cron and status-page monitors of the free-for.dev Monitoring section should the next discover unit add, after Healthchecks.io, Checkly, Pulsetic, Cronitor, Drumbeats, Phare, UptimeObserver, OnlineOrNot, StatusCake and Instatus? Take first, by the allowance the list states: Downtime Monkey (60 monitors, 5-minute interval), FlareWarden (15 monitors, 5-minute checks, 90 days of history), AlertKick (10 uptime monitors and heartbeats, 5-minute checks, 7-day retention), Xitoring (20 uptime monitors, 5 server monitors and 1 status page free; its pricing capture sha256:5f5c9a6c39c2facbbe359214ff2c1fce0ab7f6784eb161661e31bdaa7f76e0a8 names a Free plan but shows no numbers), Pingbreak (unlimited URLs), Watchgoose (10 checks), cronalive (10 checks, 50k pings a month), watchcron (5 monitors) and LastPing (unlimited monitors for individuals). Then Pingzo, Pingmeter, MonitorMonk, OpenUptime, Servervana, uptimetoolbox, sitesure.net, StatusGator, IncidentHub, pingpong.one, SweetUptime, PagerTree, Runframe, pagecrawl.io, Wachete and Accesserty Pulse. Deadman's Snitch is a settled negative that a discover unit can record as paid-only: its plans page lists Little Birdy at USD 5 a month for 3 snitches and a free trial on the top plan only, with no free plan (capture sha256:156c2efe1769d285ec46b718c68eb17416253ec61880d852e7831d9e611bd81f), where the list says one snitch is free.
why: The list line is a lead and not evidence: of the 22 vendors of the three sections whose pricing pages were read, 13 differed on at least one figure from their list line (Checkly, Pulsetic, Statsig, Amplitude, Mixpanel, Hotjar, Middleware, OpenObserve, GoatCounter, OnlineOrNot, Instatus, StatusCake, Deadman's Snitch), so each candidate needs its own pricing page read. The 26 vendors named here are the uptime, heartbeat, cron and status-page ones of the 81 that still have no record.
